#2116. One lesson Senne Lammens learned after Tottenham’s late equaliser

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Senne Lammens believes Manchester United must learn to finish games off after their late collapse against Tottenham Hotspur.

The result left the goalkeeper frustrated at Old Trafford despite leading the game and with a player more on the field.

Manchester United looked set for three points after Bryan Mbeumo put them ahead in the second half, but Dominic Solanke’s stoppage-time equaliser denied Michael Carrick’s side a much-needed victory.

Speaking to MUTV, Senne Lammens admitted the team had struggled early on but had done enough after the break to put themselves in a winning position.

“Football can be a bit cruel at times,” the Belgian goalkeeper said. “There are a lot of ups and downs, especially in a game like that.”

Senne Lammens felt United failed to take advantage of Tottenham’s red card, allowing the visitors too much space to find a late equaliser.

“We’ve won a lot of games against 10 men [in the past], but you also know there can be a tricky situation when you’re playing against 10 men, because they have nothing to lose and they know that.”

He added that United should have scored again to put the result beyond doubt or, at the very least, prevented Tottenham from creating further chances.

“I think that’s what we did wrong. We gave them a little bit too much breathing room to create those chances, and then one ball has to go right for them, one bounce has to go their way, and they can score like that.”

The goalkeeper also pointed to similarities with United’s earlier disappointment against Everton, where points slipped away late in the match.

“You feel like those games just slip away from you, and there are one or two situations where you don’t really have control,” he said.

“I think there’s a lot to learn from today. It wasn’t all negative, not at all, but especially the way it ended left a very bad feeling.”

“I think the easy answer is that we have to be able to kill the game faster and not put ourselves in that position to give them a chance.”

Despite the frustration, Lammens said there were positives to take from the performance. However, the late goal had left a bitter feeling, and United now need to turn those lessons into better results.

#2115. Crystal Palace twist hands major boost to Steve Gibson and Middlesbrough

It has been an outstanding start to the season for Middlesbrough in the Championship.

After losing to Hull City in last season's play-off final, Middlesbrough have started strongly as they look to bounce back from their Wembley heartbreak, and head coach Kim Hellberg has earned plenty of admirers for his work at the Riverside Stadium this campaign.

Middlesbrough spent big in the transfer window this summer as they look to finally secure a long-awaited return to the Premier League, and striker Will Lankshear was the club's marquee signing as he joined from Tottenham Hotspur for an initial fee of around £10 million, plus a further £10 million in add-ons.

Lankshear was not the only headline addition of the summer for Boro, with the likes of Radek Vitek, Ashley Phillips, Max Arfsten, Sebastian Berhalter, Rokas Pukstas and Kyle Joseph also arriving for significant transfer fees, and the club's ambitious squad rebuild has certainly had the desired effect so far.

It was a disappointing week for Boro before the international break as they picked up just one point from two away games at Wrexham and Watford, but while they were knocked off top spot on goal difference by Birmingham City, they currently sit second in the Championship table.

However, it seems Boro's impressive form has had some unwanted consequences for the Teesside outfit, with reports emerging over the weekend claiming that Hellberg was on the radar of top flight side Crystal Palace as they prepared to part company with Pierre Sage.

Hellberg was not the only name linked with Crystal Palace, with Thomas Frank, Frank Lampard, Sean Dyche, Vitor Pereira, Vitor Matos, Tony Popovic, Jens Berthel Askou and Ole Werner also believed to have been under consideration.

After a poor start to the season that has left them bottom of the Premier League table, the Eagles confirmed Sage's departure on Thursday after just 16 games in charge, but while Middlesbrough may have feared that the Frenchman's exit would lead to an approach for Hellberg, it seems that will not be the case.

Frank was understood to be the leading contender to replace Sage, and Palace are now reportedly in advanced talks with the former Brentford and Tottenham Hotspur boss about taking over at Selhurst Park, albeit a deal has not yet been finalised.

Given that Frank is out of work and has Premier League experience under his belt, it is easy to see why the Eagles have opted for the Dane in their current predicament, but the fact that Hellberg's name was mentioned shows that his reputation in English football is growing.

Having lost Rob Edwards to Wolverhampton Wanderers just before the November international break last season, Middlesbrough owner Steve Gibson could have been forgiven for fearing the worst when the speculation arose linking Hellberg with Crystal Palace.

In an eerie similarity to the present situation, Boro were also second in the Championship table last November when Edwards made the controversial decision to swap the Riverside Stadium for Molineux after just 16 games in charge, but it appears that history will not be repeating itself.

While Edwards was widely criticised for his response when quizzed about the Wolves job prior to his eventual departure, infamously stating that his daughter had informed him of the rumours when they first surfaced, Hellberg immediately dismissed any talk about him making the switch to Selhurst Park and insisted that he remained fully committed to Boro.

Earlier this week, when asked by Swedish outlet Fotbollskanalen how he felt about the Palace reports, Hellberg replied: "Absolutely nothing, absolutely nothing.

"It's always nice to be on lists like that, if that's the case — it shows you've done something right. But I think it's mostly just talk, and, for me, it's all about doing a good job here.

"We actually have a chance to get promoted this year. We feel that there is a chance, but then it's clear that it will be difficult.

"We are one of five, six teams, maybe not the biggest favourites, but, behind them, I think we have a good chance.

"My focus is here and hopefully we can get up, that would have been fantastic of course."

While Hellberg's loyalty to Boro has ultimately not been tested by any formal approach from the Eagles, it is clear that the 38-year-old's head has not been turned by the gossip about his future, and his comments will be music to Gibson's ears after his frustrating experience with Edwards.

Hellberg has become a hugely popular figure on Teesside over the past year, and he is regarded as one of the most exciting managers outside the Premier League, having built a team that plays an attractive, attacking brand of football, even if Boro have been a little vulnerable defensively at times this season.

Should Kim Hellberg leave Middlesbrough if a Premier League club comes calling this season? Tell us in the comments below!

Further interest in Hellberg is inevitable over the coming months if Boro continue on their current trajectory, but Gibson will be incredibly relieved to have held on to his highly-rated coach for now at least.

#2114. Manchester United defence: Why Carrick must trust Yoro and Heaven

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United endured another embarrassing draw against 10-man Tottenham after failing to register their second win despite bringing in a plethora of players.

Manchester United invested heavily last season in their attacking options, bringing in Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha.

This season, they overhauled their midfield. United spent massively on Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos. Despite spending massively, they have failed to produce the control they would have expected in the midfield. The lack of control was evident in the recent Tottenham game, where Mainoo-Tielemans partnership failed to control the game collectively.

The midfield question was covered in our recent report as well, highlighting a lack of control and carried comments from Gary Neville and Jamie Redknapp.

The bigger question is when United will strengthen their defence. As per our previous report as well, Manchester United are planning to overhaul their defence in the upcoming transfer windows.

United were heavily linked with several left backs but eventually failed to bring any one. The situation left Luke Shaw as the only senior option in the position, while Patrick Dorgu is used upfront by Michael Carrick.

Harry Amass is another option for Michael Carrick, but he is only here because of a failed transfer move. He has been rarely used at left back as Dalot and Mazraoui get the nod in the position ahead of him.

The situation at right-back isn’t all good either. Diogo Dalot is the first option there, but he rarely provides the assurance that puts Michael Carrick at ease. Noussair Mazraoui is the second choice at right-back, but his attacking numbers aren’t great either.

Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martinez form up United’s centre-back pairing while Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven are used all over the defensive line in rotation when needed. Yoro was used at right-back against Tottenham while Heaven arrived as left-back towards the end of the game.

Manchester United’s season hasn’t been defensively strong or anywhere near being good. They have conceded goals in all Premier League games and only kept one clean sheet against Sabah in the Champions League.

Lisandro Martinez has come under scrutiny after errors on four occasions. Against Ipswich Town, Manchester United won 5-2, but his error resulted in Ipswich’s second goal.

His own goal against Fulham gave away two points at Craven Cottage in the 1-1 draw. Another error led to Solanke’s goal against Tottenham, when he took his eyes off the ball.

His injury concerns are another aspect, and maybe Michael Carrick needs to make a decision.

Manchester United’s success depended heavily on youth over the years. When pundits questioned them, Sir Alex Ferguson gave them the chance to prove them wrong. Alan Hansen made the famous quote “You can’t win anything with kids” on the BBC’s Match of the Day on August 19, 1995. United did exactly that, played youth and went on to win everything.

Michael Carrick needs to do exactly that. He needs to trust youth and allow them to make mistakes. Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven arrived as massive potentials, but they haven’t been given the license to express themselves, without fearing for their places. Both the youngsters have rarely started together or in a stretch of games. It is maybe time for them to take their chances.

Michael Carrick needs to keep Harry Maguire as a senior experienced figure around them. There is no doubt over Martinez’s ability, but he is not the answer to United’s long-term problem. United need to blend youth with experience as their identity moving forward. Lisandro Martinez perhaps isn’t the answer to United’s problem.

A defensive revival expected in the upcoming transfer windows needs to happen now. It must happen with chances to the Youth. Michael Carrick needs to be brave enough and throw the youngsters in the mix. What it will bring is a long-term solution. They need to experience the errors and pressures that will shape them in football.

United have not announced any change in their managerial plans, so the report remains unconfirmed. Carrick is still in charge, but his results at the start of the new season have given the club plenty to think about.

#2111. Why must Manchester United move beyond the Glazers?

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

The Glazers took control of Manchester United in 2005. That takeover has since caused so many disruptions and protests by the fans over massive debts and insufficient backing of the team in the transfer market, despite successful periods in the Premier League and Europe.

Now Manchester United need to think about who should control the club in the future. Laurie Whitwell has now shared his views on why Manchester United need an ownership change. He simply wants the Glazers gone from Old Trafford. However, he also recognizes that replacing the current ownership doesn’t automatically mean things will improve for United.

The journalist believes the change in ownership has had a lasting effect on United, with the club still feeling its consequences today. A fresh start might be welcome, but the identity of the next owners would matter just as much as the departure of the existing ones.

“Personally, I would like to see the Glazers gone from Manchester United,” Laurie Whitwell said on The Rest is Football podcast with Gary Lineker.

“That change, you know, just really affected and still impacts United now.”

The desire for different ownership is one thing, but finding people capable of taking the club forward is another.

Whitwell admitted there is no perfect answer when it comes to who should take charge.

That leaves United facing a difficult choice. A sale could offer the chance to change how the club is run, but simply bringing in a new owner would not guarantee better decisions or a brighter future.

Whitwell also raised the idea of United supporters having a greater say in the club’s ownership and decisions, much like the Barcelona model where fans own the club itself. However, he highlighted that the Barcelona model isn’t ideal either and has its own shortcomings.

Changing the names at the top would only be one part of the change. The club would also need an ownership structure capable of making sound decisions and providing a direction.

The issue of ownership goes beyond whether the Glazers should stay or leave. Manchester United needs to find the right people and the right model to secure the club’s future. Getting that decision wrong could leave them facing the same circus the fans are enduring under the Glazers.

For Norwich City, it will feel as though the international break came at the completely wrong time as Philippe Clement's side began to hit their stride in the Championship.

Although nowhere near the levels of last season's dire start under Liam Manning, the Belgian was still the subject of intense criticism before the start of a current four-game winning run in which 15 goals have been netted.

The Canaries are now 12th in the table as a result, just four places and three points behind the expanded play-off places, which is exactly where many outsiders predicted them to finish in pre-season.

The experienced head coach has battled against many injuries to key players, but the aforementioned run to form has come slightly after Jovon Makama's return to full fitness following two frustrating setbacks.

In a short sample size of minutes, the 22-year-old has reminded everyone of his qualities, and it has drawn particularly high praise from a Carrow Road legend.

Makama was one of several summer arrivals during Manning's only transfer window in Norfolk, penning a five-year contract after a £1.2m deal was struck with Lincoln City.

Having amassed 15 goal contributions for the Imps in 2025/26, many were intrigued to see how the attacker fared in the Championship, although, like many of his teammates, it took until Clement's arrival for his season to kickstart.

Despite netting three times under the Belgian's predecessor, Makama's first purple patch at Carrow Road came between November 2025 and January 2026, in which he netted eight times in 10 Championship outings, with Norwich winning four of those encounters.

Norwich won three of the following four games with Makama as one of their attacking focal points, but it then transpired that the highly-rated forward would miss the remainder of the season.

One of two foot injuries was the root cause of his absence, which has since led to Clement adopting a cautious outlook on the forward's minutes at the beginning of the current campaign.

Philippe Clement has deployed Lucien Mahovo further forward, despite emerging as a left-back, which is a mirror image of Thomas Meunier's career

Makama's first game back after seven months injured came in the 2-1 victory over Birmingham City on September 9th, but just one start so far this season has limited his impact to just 347 minutes' worth of action.

Makama recently hailed Clement for the impact he has had on the striker's performances despite such injury woes, saying: “I think Philippe Clement coming in has helped me develop massively as well, and there’s still a lot more to come."

In those 10 appearances, the England youth international has scored his first three goals of the season, including a stunning effort in the 4-0 rout at Derby County on November 3rd, before also netting against Bristol City last time out.

As such, the striker was called up to Lee Carsley's England Under-21s squad for the first time for friendlies against Portugal and France, and whilst his involvement in said matches remains to be seen, it has seen the Nottingham native receive high praise indeed from Canaries cult hero, Iwan Roberts.

Discussing who could be in line to replace the Three Lions' all-time record goalscorer, appearance holder and Ballon d'Or winner, Harry Kane, the Welshman said: “But who's next on the conveyor belt? Who's next in line? Obviously, people are talking about Will Lankshear, after his £10m move to Middlesbrough. He got 13 goals this season and he's the name on the end of everybody's tongue at the minute.

Lisandro Martinez has held discussions with Jason Wilcox and Michael Carrick after speaking out following United’s 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid.

Martinez had questioned whether Carrick was backed enough in the summer and suggested the club needed changes.

Fabrizio Romano has now confirmed that United consider the matter resolved for now and expect Martinez to remain available for selection.

Speaking about the situation on his YouTube channel, as quoted by Football 365, Romano explained why Martinez’s comments caused concern inside the club.

“He spoke very strongly after the game against Atletico Madrid, which Man Utd lost. It was a very negative moment for the Red Devils. We know that Licha was very strong in his comments. He said that Michael Carrick was not backed enough during the summer transfer window.”

Romano added that Martinez had spoken directly to those at the club after the incident.

“Licha apologised to Man Utd as a club. He spoke to the directors, he spoke to Jason Wilcox, and he spoke to Michael Carrick, who was also involved in this conversation.”

“So, the underlying message remains the same. Lisandro is apologising for the way he expressed himself after a game during a difficult moment for Man Utd, but there was a discussion about the substance of what he said.”

Romano also revealed that United had imposed a financial penalty on the centre-back. However, the punishment does not appear to involve removing him from the squad.

“According to the information available tonight, Lisandro Martinez has been fined.”

He added that Martinez is expected to return to the squad as normal, with the fine considered sufficient punishment for the incident.

“The internal discussion also helped to resolve all the issues. For Man Utd, the case is closed.”

That should bring some immediate clarity to the situation, although questions remain about how the episode could affect Martinez’s longer-term position at Old Trafford.

Romano also pointed towards Martinez’s contract, which expires next summer, with United holding an option to extend it.

“So, let’s see what is going to happen there. For sure, this is the kind of situation that will have an impact on the situation surrounding Lisandro, but we have to see what happens next in terms of future transfers and everything else.”

#2105. Wolves tied Kieran Trippier down until 2028 – now comes a difficult decision

Wolves are in a good position as they look to bounce back to the Premier League at the first attempt.

It was a strange summer at Molineux, with Rob Edwards surprisingly dismissed for Cesar Peixoto, and the squad overhaul that many anticipated didn’t come to fruition.

However, to their credit, Wolves did manage to secure two statement signings early in the window, as Raul Jimenez and Kieran Trippier joined the club as free agents.

Both deals were seen as huge coups for the Championship side, as both players featured in the Premier League last season, and they have had excellent careers.

And, especially in the case of Trippier, it saw Wolves addressing what had been a problem position, with Jackson Tchatchoua having endured a miserable first season in English football as the team were relegated last season.

But, with Trippier 36, Peixoto has had to manage the minutes of the former Newcastle man carefully, with the need to do that reinforced after the right-back suffered an injury in the opening day draw against Blackburn that ruled him out for a month.

Since then, it has been noticeable that Trippier only played twice in the three-game weeks that Wanderers have had.

That meant he watched on as Wolves beat Burnley last month, and he was also an unused substitute in the draw at Wrexham last time out, having played 90 minutes against Cardiff and Bristol City prior to that.

Many will see this as sensible management from Peixoto, but it shows the challenges the Portuguese head coach faces, as he will recognise just how important Trippier is to the team.

FLW names its Team of the Season so far in the Championship

Despite his age, Trippier remains a decent one-vs-one defender, even if he has struggled at times, with Tommy Conway giving him a tough time in Wolves’ defeat at Middlesbrough.

On the whole, though, even though he lacks pace, Trippier’s intelligence and positional play means he always knows what to do, and he plays a key role in ensuring Wolves are solid at the back.

Then, on the ball, he remains a fantastic player. Whether it’s finding the channels or pinging balls into the feet of attacking players, there are few defenders at this level who have the technical ability of the former England international, who is crucial to the way Wolves build up play.

When you add in his devastating delivery that has already brought rewards, it’s no exaggeration to say that Trippier is one of the most important players in the Wolves squad, even though his best days are behind him - and that's without discussing his leadership qualities.

Yet, as outlined above, Peixoto must pick and choose the games that Trippier plays, so backup right-back Jackson Tchatchoua is going to get a lot of minutes this season.

He has already featured in nine Championship games, and the low point undoubtedly came in the 2-2 draw at Birmingham City, where he inexplicably fired the ball past Jose Sa to score an own goal.

But, since then, Tchatchoua has been solid if unspectacular, with his electric pace meaning he is very difficult to beat.

However, his quality on the ball is incomparable to Trippier, so it certainly restricts the way Wolves can play when the ex-Verona man starts.

That is another reason why Trippier’s minutes will be carefully selected, as a long-term lay-off could have major implications, even if Tchatchoua has been steady when called upon since the mistake at St. Andrew’s.

Trippier’s age and fitness issues mean Peixoto is always having to look ahead, and with the demands of the Championship clear, he has probably mapped out how he wants to use the full-back with the player.

That will be particularly important in the latter part of the campaign, as Peixoto is going to want Trippier, who has captained the team on occasions, to be out there in the biggest games.

Looking beyond this season, though, it shows Wolves face a dilemma in the summer, as they signed Trippier on a two-year contract.

If they remain in the Championship, it wouldn’t be a major surprise if the same situation played out, with Tchatchoua, or a new signing, acting as deputy to Trippier.

But, promotion could change the outlook considerably. Firstly, there aren’t as many games, so, in theory, Trippier could play more regularly as he won’t be required to play three times a week very often.

Nevertheless, there will be doubts about his ability to cope in the Premier League, so Trippier may go from a key player to someone on the fringes, which could impact the dynamic in the dressing room.

Will Wolves win promotion this season? Let us know in the comments below.

So, that’s something to monitor, and Wolves will hope it’s a problem they have to deal with later on, as the only priority right now is winning promotion back to the Premier League.

Trippier will be integral to their chances of doing that - although his age means that Tchatchoua is going to have a bigger role to play than many perhaps envisaged as well.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

Manchester United had a difficult evening once again as they were held to a 1-1 draw at Leeds United. Pressure mounts on Michael Carrick as United have just 7 points from 7 games.

Manchester United took the lead through Bryan Mbeumo in the first half, with the forward finishing Youri Tielemans’ excellent cross from the right. However, the visitors couldn’t hold on to their advantage as Dominic Calvert-Lewin equalised for Leeds United from a corner.

The draw extended United’s frustrating run of results, leaving Michael Carrick still searching for the consistency his side need.

Jamie Carragher has singled out Harry Maguire for praise after Manchester United drew 1-1 with Leeds United at Elland Road on Sunday.

Speaking on Sky Sports, the former Liverpool defender admitted that picking up a point at Elland Road was not necessarily a bad result in isolation, even if United’s recent form made it feel like a missed opportunity.

“Going away to Leeds is going to be tricky for any team except for Manchester City and Arsenal at the moment,” Carragher said.

#2100. Mark Robins can land Stoke City £200m+ jackpot - Coventry City fans will like it

In recent times, there haven't exactly been many reasons to be cheerful for those of a Stoke City persuasion.

The Potters' recent stagnation in the Championship across a near decade's worth of action has been well-documented, with it coming so soon after a strong period in which the club was established in the Premier League.

The Bet365 Stadium had, rather notoriously, become one of the hardest places in the top-flight for some of English football's elite to take three points from, especially due to the North Staffordshire climate and hostilities.

Those times could certainly be returning in the near future, with Mark Robins getting plenty of locals excited about the remainder of the Championship season - a feat which Coventry City supporters know all too well.

Stoke, despite their reputation in the Premier League's modern era, haven't come close to ending their exile from the top-flight since being relegated eight years ago.

The Reds have gone through seven managers during that timeframe, with the first of those - Gary Rowett - particularly unable to deal with the pressure of the club being pre-season promotion favourites at the first time of asking,

As well as retaining many of the squad which had been relegated, Stoke invested over £50m in new players in 2018, much of which was wasted given the lack of impact made by the likes of Tom Ince and Benik Afobe.

Ryan Woods' move to the Potteries was the start of an unfortunate decline for the midfielder

There have since been further false dawns under Michael O'Neill, the club's longest-serving manager in said timeframe, whilst Alex Neil, Steven Schumacher and Narcis Pelach also couldn't reverse City's fortunes prior to Robins' arrival last January, two months after he was somewhat controversially dismissed by Coventry.

Robins is now in the thick of a seventh managerial spell, but his second stint with the Sky Blues between March 2017 and November 2024 is, unarguably, what makes his body of work so impressive.

Coventry's recently chequered past saw the club groundshare on two occasions with Northampton Town and Birmingham City, whilst the club were relegated to League Two shortly after his reappointment despite winning the EFL Trophy in April 2017.

Despite boycotts from supporters due to Sisu's day-to-day running of the club, Robins was able to galvanise the majority of the fanbase and his ever-changing squads in CV6 as they enjoyed quite the rise in such a short space of time.

After winning the fourth tier play-offs at the first attempt, City found themselves back in the Championship just two years later despite being exiled in Birmingham.

During this period, Robins unearthed gems such as Viktor Gyökeres and Gustavo Hamer, who both went on to make the club significant cash after the Sky Blues' agonising Championship play-off final penalty shootout loss to Luton Town in May 2023, which was followed by more Wembley heartache as the then-second tier side lost on spot kicks to Manchester United in the FA Cup semi-final.

Pick any two players. Send the code, and your mate enters it here to play the same pair.

Ultimately, though, the 56-year-old laid the groundwork for Coventry's eventual Premier League return under Frank Lampard in May, with many of his recruits now adapting to life in the top division.

Whilst the scale of Robins' rebuilding jobs at Coventry and Stoke cannot be fully compared, the experienced head coach has surprised many by the fact only goal difference is denying the Potters from leading the Championship at present.

Regardless of selling former creator-in-chief, Sorba Thomas, to Hull City, the Reds have recruited extremely smartly this season, with the likes of Luke Graham, Djibril Soumare, Ethan Galbraith, Justin Devenney and Jack McGlynn all earning rave reviews.

Stoke fans, how optimistic are you of achieving promotion under Mark Robins? Comment below!

More has been expected from fellow summer recruit, George Hirst, but it is an encouraging start for a club who have finished no higher than 14th since relegation.

However, Stoke fans will also be cautious of the fact that exactly a year ago their side sat third in the Championship on 27 points behind Coventry and Middlesbrough, before a run of just five wins in the second half of the season contributed to a major fall down the standings.

“Manchester United were in for him, 100%, but the fee was just too much,” he added.

Ferdinand was left frustrated by what he saw from the teenager, who turned 19 this month.

“Just that little cameo against PSG makes you go, ‘oh, I can’t believe we missed out on that. I can’t believe it.’ I’m so gutted, so gutted. He’s bad! He’s so calm under pressure.”

Rio Ferdinand suggested Bouaddi’s quality could soon make the midfield position in a packed Manchester City his regular role.

City already have Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez among their midfield options, but Ferdinand believes Bouaddi has the ability to stand out alongside them.

“They’ve got Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez in that midfield as well but this kid could be the best of the three, easily.”

#2098. Michael Carrick handed lifeline ahead of Chelsea trip

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Michael Carrick has come under immense pressure as a disjointed Manchester United sit just two places above the relegation places.

Despite the scrutiny and the news of a possible sacking, Michael Carrick has been given another chance at Manchester United.

Michael Carrick will remain in charge of Manchester United for their Premier League trip to Chelsea on Saturday after the club decided to give their under-pressure head coach another opportunity to turn things around.

United have gone eight games without a win in all competitions, with Sunday’s humiliating 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth leaving them 16th in the Premier League table, just one point above the relegation zone.

Carrick’s position looked increasingly uncertain after the Bournemouth loss. As a result, United chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox were at Carrington on Monday to discuss the situation.

It has been reported by Sky Sports that United have considered other options internally as well to replace Micahel Carrick but for the weekend, they are sticking with Michael Carrick.

Carrick took training on Tuesday and the decision means he has at least one more match to convince the club’s hierarchy that he can get United back on track.

Gary Neville admitted he was surprised that Carrick had survived the immediate threat of losing his job, although he welcomed the decision.

“I am surprised, but I am happy because I was absolutely certain that what I witnessed on Sunday would be the end of Michael,” Neville said in Sky Sports.

The former United captain explained that Carrick’s actions after the Bournemouth defeat had made him think the manager was preparing to say goodbye to the supporters.

“It looked like he was walking round at the end on his own with the players behind him, like it was almost a goodbye lap,” Neville added.

Fans continued singing the manager’s name after the final whistle, while the rest of the team drew boos.

Despite his surprise, Gary Neville hopes Micahel Carrick can use the extra time to get a response from his squad.

“I hope he can somehow get those players to start playing for him again because they haven’t played for him in the last few weeks,” he said.

The trip to Chelsea now becomes a crucial test for Micahel Carrick but United need a result and a far better performance to ease the pressure at Old Trafford.

#2095. Two days or two weeks – Michael Carrick future decision rolls into the international break

Manchester United will use the November international break to decide whether Michael Carrick stays on as head coach, after a three-game reprieve that delivered only one win.

According to The Guardian, Carrick came close to being sacked after the 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth on 25 October.

Director of football Jason Wilcox and chief executive Omar Berrada discussed his position at the training ground the following day and agreed to give him three matches to turn things around before the break.

Those games brought a 2-0 defeat at Chelsea, a 3-2 win over Roma and a chaotic 4-4 draw with Aston Villa at Old Trafford on Sunday. United conceded eight goals across the three fixtures, and defensive frailty remains the biggest worry.

Wilcox is now leading a review of Carrick’s position. He will consult Berrada before making a recommendation to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, who oversees the club’s sporting operations. Talks are expected to begin on Monday and continue through the break.

The league table makes grim reading. United sit in the Premier League relegation zone with just one league win in their last 10 matches.

If he does win a stay of execution, results will need to follow. Manchester United cannot be languishing in 17th place.

Carrick remains defiant. Speaking to Sky Sports News after the Villa draw, he admitted his side “haven’t won enough games” but insisted he expects to move forward.

“I’m quite clear with what direction the club needs to go in, and it’s got to win games, said Carrick after the late Villa draw.

“I think there’s more than enough [to turn things around].”

If United do make a change, former Newcastle manager Eddie Howe is reported to be Wilcox’s preferred candidate. Howe has been out of work since leaving St James’ Park during pre-season, after four and a half years in charge.

In the meantime, there are no plans to strengthen Carrick’s coaching staff.

For now, Carrick is expected to be in charge for United’s next match, against Liverpool. Whether three games were enough to convince the hierarchy should become clear before then.

The trip to Anfield could be do or die for the decorated former United midfielder.

He’s not likely to survive a heavy defeat at the home of the club’s fierce rivals, but a galvanising win would surely buy him time and goodwill.

That’s if he makes it through the next fortnight before then. A decision or indication could be two days or two weeks away.

The only certainty at Old Trafford is uncertainty.

#2094. Scott Parker could reverse a West Ham decision that angered Nuno's bosses

A new era is underway at West Ham United following the appointment of Scott Parker as the club's new head coach.

After spending four years at the club as a player, Parker returned to West Ham as head coach when he replaced Nuno Espirito Santo last week, but it has not been the start to his tenure at the London Stadium that he would have hoped.

Parker's reign at West Ham got off to a nightmare start as his side found themselves 3-0 down at half time in his first game in charge at Cardiff City last Wednesday night, but they produced a stunning second half comeback to draw the game 3-3.

If Parker was hoping that the Hammers would carry that momentum into their next match, that certainly did not prove to be the case as they slumped to a disappointing 2-1 defeat at Blackburn Rovers on Saturday.

West Ham head into the November international break sitting in ninth in the Championship table, one point outside the play-off places and six points from the automatic promotion spots, and Parker will be keen to pick up his first victory at the third attempt when bottom side Preston North End visit the London Stadium next week.

Given his previous connection to the club, and the fact that he has won promotion from the Championship on three occasions with Fulham, Bournemouth and Burnley, it is easy to see why the Hammers turned to Parker after parting company with Nuno, and the 46-year-old may have an early opportunity to impress his new bosses.

While West Ham were widely expected to win the Championship title this season, there was plenty of shock at the club's brutal decision to sack Nuno last week, despite sitting just four points from the automatic promotion places at the time of his exit.

Back-to-back home defeats to two fellow promotion hopefuls in Southampton and West Bromwich Albion were the final straw for the Hammers' hierarchy, but it seems they may have had growing doubts about Nuno for some time, including some of his selection calls.

West Ham signed midfielder Edson Alvarez from Ajax for a fee of around £35 million in August 2023, but after he spent last season on loan with Turkish giants Fenerbahçe, many assumed he would leave the London Stadium this summer following the club's relegation.

It was, therefore, something of a surprise when Alvarez failed to score a move away before the end of the summer window, but despite remaining in East London, he was almost entirely overlooked by Nuno, making just one EFL Cup appearance and being left out of all of his Championship matchday squads.

Another midfielder who found himself out in the cold under Nuno was Soungoutou Magassa, who made 26 appearances in his debut campaing with the Hammers last season after arriving from French outfit Monaco for a fee of around £17.3 million.

Magassa did not make a single league or cup appearance under Nuno prior to his depature last week, but, unlike Alvarez, he was included in a handful of matchday squads in the Championship.

It seems that Nuno's bizarre selection calls involving Alvarez and Magassa did not go down well with the West Ham hierarchy, with The Guardian revealing that his reluctance to use the latter in particular had caused "disquiet" at the club, both because his absence meant that he was being "devalued" and a vulnerable defence was "going without enough protection".

While West Ham are the top scorers in the Championship, having netted 37 goals so far this season, they have also conceded 23 goals, which is the most of any side in the top half of the table other than 12th-placed Norwich City.

Under-fire goalkeeper Mads Hermansen and the Hammers' fragile backline have come under plenty of scrutiny in recent weeks, but there is no doubt that Nuno's refusal to play a holding midfielder significantly contributed to his side's defensive woes and his own personal downfall.

Nuno may have understandably been disappointed that Alvarez and Magassa both sought exits from the London Stadium this summer, but after both were still present at the club when the transfer window closed, he should have made use of the pair.

Alvarez has spent much of his career at the top level of European football, while he made four appearances for Mexico at this summer's World Cup, including in England's famous 3-2 victory at the Azteca in July, so the 29-year-old would surely be capable of doing a job in the Championship.

Magassa struggled to make an impact at times during his first year at West Ham last season, but he was far from the only player to underperform as the club were relegated from the Premier League, and it is difficult not to feel that a player of his potential could also have a role to play in the second tier.

Should Edson Alvarez and Soungoutou Magassa be regular starters for West Ham United under Scott Parker? Tell us in the comments below!

Parker brought Magassa back into the fold for his first game in charge at Cardiff last week, handing him a surprise start before taking him off at the break, and he was an unused substitute in the defeat at Blackburn last time out, while Alvarez was left out of the matchday squad for both games.

Hammers fans have long been calling for Alvarez and Magassa to be given a chance to solve their side's midfield problems, and with the club's hierarchy seemingly sharing that view, Parker should focus on reintegrating the duo over the international break.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#2093. Chelsea World Cup Knockout Load Gives Xabi Alonso Pre-Season Problem

Chelsea’s World Cup contingent has moved from a group-stage watchlist into a genuine Xabi Alonso planning problem.

Chelsea’s own tournament update confirms that Enzo Fernandez, Mike Penders, Moises Caicedo, Kendry Paez, Malo Gusto and Jorrel Hato have reached the Round of 32.

England have also progressed after their final Group L win over Panama, which keeps Reece James and Trevoh Chalobah inside the wider knockout picture.

For supporters, that is a status marker. For Alonso, it is where summer pride starts to become pre-season compression.

The concern is not simply volume. It is where the minutes are landing.

Enzo has not missed a minute for Argentina, while Caicedo has remained central for Ecuador and captained them in the 2-1 win over Germany.

Those are not fringe workloads. They are the two midfield profiles Chelsea have built large parts of their control game around.

Alonso’s first Chelsea pre-season was always going to demand clarity through the middle of the pitch.

Instead, the players most central to that reset are still operating in knockout football.

Caicedo’s Ecuador role is the cleanest example. Read Chelsea has already assessed how his captaincy display against Germany strengthened his leadership case, but the next layer is more complicated.

Every additional knockout tie gives him more tournament rhythm, more authority and more fatigue.

Argentina’s route against Cape Verde keeps him on a glamorous stage at exactly the moment Chelsea need to settle his role, mood and tactical responsibilities under Alonso.

If Madrid-related noise continues around him, the club cannot afford a sluggish July handover.

Reece James started England’s first two matches before a hamstring issue ruled him out of the Panama game, according to the Guardian.

England still topped the group and moved into a last-32 tie with DR Congo, but James’ situation is exactly the kind of detail Chelsea’s medical team will monitor closely.

Chelsea have already had to plan around a large World Cup group.

The broader issue was clear in Read Chelsea’s earlier pre-season workload piece, but the knockout stage sharpens it because the returns will now be staggered.

Enzo brings a maximum group-stage load. Caicedo brings captaincy responsibility and heavy Ecuador minutes.

James brings knockout qualification mixed with another hamstring-management question.

Gusto and Hato remain tied to France and the Netherlands, while Penders and Paez are still absorbing tournament environments before club reintegration.

That is a spine issue, not a fringe issue.

Alonso needs automatisms in possession, spacing around the double pivot, clearer full-back behaviour and pressing triggers from midfield.

Those details do not bed in properly when key players arrive in drips after a major summer tournament.

Players returning from knockout football can bring competitive sharpness that closed-door friendlies cannot replicate.

Caicedo captaining Ecuador through pressure games matters. Enzo playing high-leverage minutes for Argentina matters.

Gusto and Hato absorbing tournament detail also helps Chelsea’s defensive reset.

But Chelsea cannot treat every tournament minute as clean preparation.

Alonso must decide who returns straight into tactical work, who needs a genuine pause and who can handle August without creating an avoidable injury bill by September.

That is where the James situation feels central.

If Chelsea’s captain carries a World Cup hamstring warning, the club’s right-sided structure becomes more than a selection debate.

It becomes an availability question that touches Gusto, the wider defensive rebuild and the need for control from midfield.

Read Chelsea has already looked at James’ captaincy test under Alonso, and the injury layer now makes that test sharper.

This is the hidden cost of a strong international footprint.

Chelsea want players good enough to survive deep into tournaments.

Alonso now has to make sure that status does not leave his first league weeks short of the very control those players are meant to provide.

#2092. Monaco summit adds unnecessary drama to Michael Carrick situation

Michael Carrick arrived at Carrington for Manchester United training as normal on Tuesday morning, while his bosses were preparing to decide his future in talks on the Mediterranean.

Chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox are flying to Monaco to meet Sir Jim Ratcliffe, with the BBC reporting that the pair will recommend Carrick is sacked.The Guardian has indicated representatives of the Glazer family will also be involved.

The club insists the Monaco summit was pre-planned and is not solely about the head coach and while that may be true, it hardly matters.By allowing the meeting to become public knowledge, United have turned a straightforward football decision into unnecessary drama, compounding an already difficult situation.

What does is say about Man United in 2026 that a manager is given three games to secure his job, then left to train the squad during an international break while the executives are flying off to rule on his future? It’s farcical.

The latest chapter is another muddled process.Wilcox and Berrada met at Carrington the day after the 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth on 25 October and agreed to give Carrick three more matches.A defeat at Chelsea, a win over Roma and a 4-4 draw with Aston Villa later, they appear to have reached the conclusion many expected a fortnight ago.

If the timeline holds, the decision will be made at Wednesday’s meeting, with an official announcement expected later in the week.United reportedly want to tell Carrick face to face, which means he could spend another day or two working under a cloud. In reality, it could be two days or two weeks.

The stakes could hardly be higher. United have won once in 10 league games, their worst-ever start to a Premier League season, and sit one point off the bottom in 18th place.

Should Carrick go, attention will turn quickly to his successor.ESPN reports that United States head coach Mauricio Pochettino is the favoured candidate, while Eddie Howe has been named as Wilcox’s preferred choice. Antonio Conte has also been mentioned.

Carrick deserves better than this.Whatever the outcome, a club that wants to be taken seriously should not be settling its manager’s future in the full glare of the media while he is still out on the training pitch.

#2091. Malo Gusto’s Kante Lesson Gives Chelsea A £75m Xabi Alonso Decision

Malo Gusto’s World Cup has suddenly become more than a France subplot for Chelsea. It is now a live assessment of whether Xabi Alonso inherits a right-back worth protecting, reshaping or trading at the peak of his market.

Chelsea’s own interview with Gusto this week underlined the human part of that equation. The 23-year-old spoke about learning from N’Golo Kante, calling the former Blue one of the best midfielders France have produced and stressing the value of his example on and off the pitch.

That matters because Kante is not just a nostalgic reference point. He remains the standard Chelsea supporters still use when judging humility, intensity and reliability in a high-pressure dressing room.

For Gusto, those qualities arrive at a decisive moment. Reports around the player’s future claim Chelsea value him at around £75million, with the imminent Marco Palestra deal creating a more crowded full-back picture.

That number looks aggressive, but the logic is clear. Gusto is young, capped by France, under contract, Premier League-tested and capable of playing in several defensive structures.

🚨🚨| NEW: Chelsea are open to selling Malo Gusto this summer, with his agent already in 𝐓𝐀𝐋𝐊𝐒 with Manchester City and Inter. Chelsea will only sell if their valuation is met.{@siphillipssport} pic.twitter.com/vNR2bWud9F

The easiest reading of Gusto’s Kante comments is sentimental. It should not be.

For Alonso, who officially begins work on July 1, the important detail is what those comments say about the player Chelsea have been developing.

Gusto has not always looked completely settled at Stamford Bridge. His best games have carried thrust, speed and recovery power, while his less convincing spells have raised questions about final-ball quality and defensive concentration.

That uncertainty is exactly why the next coach matters.

Alonso’s previous teams have leaned heavily on wide players who can receive under pressure, attack space early and still protect the back line when possession breaks down. Gusto has the athletic base for that job.

The test is whether his decision-making can be refined enough to make him a structural piece rather than a rotation asset.

That is where the Kante reference lands with force. Chelsea do not need Gusto to imitate Kante’s position. They need him to absorb the same professional standard: repeat actions, clean defensive choices, no wasted emotion and total commitment to the collective rhythm.

The Marco Palestra deal changes the right side of Chelsea’s squad immediately. Read Chelsea has already examined how Palestra’s arrival offers a tactical clue over Alonso’s defensive plans, and that pressure is now sharpened by market noise around Gusto.

Chelsea can frame the situation in two ways.

One is profit-led. If a club comes close to the reported £75million level, selling a player signed from Lyon for a much lower fee becomes a powerful PSR lever.

The other is football-led. If Alonso sees Gusto as a high-upside wing-back who fits his model, selling him just as the coaching environment becomes more suitable would carry long-term risk.

The complication is Reece James. The captain’s fitness issues, including his current England hamstring concern, mean Chelsea still need genuine right-sided depth.

Palestra may be part of the future, but Gusto is already part of the present. Chelsea have too often needed emergency solutions in that area to treat proven depth lightly.

That is why Read Chelsea’s recent look at James awaiting hamstring scan results matters in this debate. Right-back remains one of the most talented areas of the squad, but also one of the least straightforward.

This is why Gusto’s France rhythm is more valuable than a simple tournament diary entry. Chelsea are watching a player operate inside an elite international camp, learn from a club legend and handle a public transfer valuation that can change his status overnight.

Alonso’s first decision does not have to be final, but it does have to be clear.

If Gusto stays, he needs a defined role early in pre-season and a pathway that makes sense alongside Palestra and James. If Chelsea sell, they need to do it at a number that justifies weakening one of the few squad areas where youth, speed and top-level experience already overlap.

Gusto’s Kante lesson, then, is not just a feel-good Chelsea connection. It is a reminder of the standard Alonso must demand before deciding whether £75million is a price to accept or a warning sign that Chelsea should hold firm.

#2090. Stand-outs for good and bad reasons: Fan player ratings from Genoa 1-2 AC Milan

AC Milan ensured they will go into the international break in good spirits as they beat Genoa 2-1 away from home on Sunday.

Milan led by two goals inside 20 minutes after Alphadjo Cisse slotted in a cut-back from Adrien Rabiot to get his eighth of the campaign, before Christian Pulisic buried a square pass from Gonçalo Ramos after a stray pass inside the box.

Ellertsson scored with a strike from distance inside the final few minutes to make it a nervy finale, but Milan did ultimately manage to hang on for what was an important three points that moves them back into the top four.

We published our player ratings just after the full-time whistle which we would always urge you to read first, while the Italian newspapers have given their verdict on what was another game of two halves from Milan.

Starting with the positive notes, there were four players who scored a 7 or higher on average. The goal scorers Cisse (7.0) and Pulisic (7.6) were unsurprisingly two of them, but Adrien Rabiot (7.3) and Koni De Winter (7.1) were also judged to have done their bit.

Luka Modric isn’t far behind with a 6.9, while Mike Maignan follows him with a 6.8. Mario Gila got a 6.5, Sankhoun Diawara a 6.3, Diego Moreira a 6.6 and Yunus Musah a 6.1. Gonçalo Ramos (5.9) was the only starter to get below a passing grade.

The substitutes are a different story, as has often been the case. Filippo Terracciano and Ardon Jashari were both awarded a 5.5. Omari Hutchinson scored 5.0, and Pervis Estupinan was deemed worthy of a 4.6 on average.

#2088. Senegal Knockout Tie Gives Chelsea A Double Xabi Alonso Audit

Chelsea’s World Cup watch has moved beyond simple minutes management.

Senegal’s Round-of-32 meeting with Belgium now gives Xabi Alonso a live read on two very different development tracks.

Nicolas Jackson’s attacking authority is the immediate question. Mamadou Sarr’s defensive readiness is the longer-term one.

Chelsea confirmed that Senegal kept their knockout hopes alive with a 5-0 win over Iraq, with Jackson featuring from the bench.

Senegal have since moved into the knockouts, where they face Belgium in Seattle on Wednesday 1 July.

Jackson and Sarr travel into that game with contrasting club questions attached. Both still carry clear Chelsea relevance.

Sarr has not been the loudest Chelsea story of the tournament.

That may actually make this test more useful.

The 20-year-old is still moving through the awkward stage between prospect, squad option and saleable BlueCo asset.

Knockout football against Belgium can sharpen that picture quickly.

The timing is awkward in the best possible way for Chelsea. Alonso steps into a squad with expensive centre-backs, academy-trained options and a board still comfortable using the market aggressively.

A disciplined Sarr performance would not end that search. It would give the recruitment team a stronger internal benchmark before committing another major fee.

Chelsea need defenders who can hold a high line, cover wide channels and still pass through pressure. Belgium should ask those questions more directly than most group-stage opponents.

The context matters. Chelsea’s recall note recorded that Sarr returned from Strasbourg after 18 appearances across Ligue 1 and the Conference League.

The club also noted that he had already earned his first Senegal cap.

That is a different profile from an academy player being carried by reputation alone.

There is a statistical base behind the interest too. When Chelsea completed the deal, beIN SPORTS noted that Sarr made 27 Ligue 1 appearances in his first Strasbourg season.

He helped them keep 10 clean sheets. He also produced a team-high 20 blocks and made 25 interceptions.

Those numbers explain why this Belgium game is not just a sentimental World Cup subplot.

Alonso’s Chelsea defence is already crowded with Levi Colwill, Wesley Fofana, Trevoh Chalobah and external targets still orbiting the plan.

ReadChelsea has already looked at why Colwill’s recovery story gives Alonso a defensive test. Sarr’s value is different.

He is still being evaluated as a physical, long-range defensive project.

Jackson’s role changes the editorial weight of the tie.

Chelsea’s striker picture has been messy for long enough. Any high-pressure international performance now carries wider meaning.

ReadChelsea has already framed the forward’s tournament as a live Senegal striker audit for Chelsea.

Belgium should stress both Chelsea questions at once.

Jackson has to offer penalty-box threat and transition security. Sarr, if trusted, has to defend space against a technically cleaner opponent.

He also has to show whether his recovery pace and frame translate under tournament pressure.

Sarr’s own mentality profile is worth noting. In a Chelsea World Cup Q&A, he named Lionel Messi, Sadio Mane and Paul Pogba as his tournament heroes.

His answer on Pogba focused on leadership and group mentality.

That lands neatly with the exact question Chelsea now need answered. Is there enough presence to go with the physical tools?

This is why Belgium feels like a pathway check rather than a routine World Cup watch item.

Chelsea do not need Sarr to solve the defence in July. They need clearer evidence on whether he belongs in Alonso’s first pre-season group.

He could need another loan. He could also become part of the club’s centre-back market arithmetic.

For Jackson, the question is more immediate. For Sarr, it is more structural.

Together, Senegal’s knockout tie gives Chelsea a rare clean look at two players on opposite ends of the same squad-building argument.

Who can help now, and who is worth protecting for later?

#2087. Michael Olise Gives Chelsea A Hard Xabi Alonso Wide-Player Benchmark

Michael Olise has moved from former Chelsea academy footnote to genuine Ballon d’Or conversation piece.

That should land at Cobham as more than a wistful what-if.

Bavarian Football Works relayed comments from former Chelsea and France winger Florent Malouda, who described the Bayern Munich forward as a live Ballon d’Or contender if France turn their World Cup run into silverware.

The point is not simply that Chelsea once had Olise in the building. It is that his rise provides a hard benchmark for the type of final-third specialist Xabi Alonso must either develop or buy.

Chelsea have spent heavily on attacking upside. Olise’s rise is a reminder that the real separator is not potential, but repeatable elite production.

Bayern’s own season review underlines why the conversation has accelerated.

The German champions confirmed Olise finished 2025/26 with 25 goals and 28 assists from 57 competitive appearances. He was also named Bayern’s Player of the Season for a second straight year, finishing ahead of Harry Kane and Luis Diaz in the fan vote.

That is elite production from a wide creator who does not play like a chalk-on-boots winger.

Olise can receive wide, drift inside, manipulate the half-space and still deliver the last pass at match-winning speed. Chelsea have bought attackers with pieces of that profile, but few have joined the dots with that level of consistency.

There is an obvious recruitment lesson here.

The market will now price that blend of creativity, ball security and goal threat close to superstar territory. If Chelsea want an Alonso attack that controls games rather than simply runs through them, the next winger decision cannot be judged on pace or upside alone.

It has to be judged on game control, final-third calm and repeat output.

The World Cup has sharpened the comparison.

Chelsea’s official France preview noted that Malo Gusto was in the same squad as N’Golo Kante and former Blues academy player Olise. It was a neat reminder of how many Chelsea strands sit inside Didier Deschamps’ group.

Bundesliga’s tournament analysis was even more revealing. It noted that Olise had reached 10 France goal involvements in 18 appearances and was named Player of the Match on his World Cup debut against Senegal.

That same analysis highlighted the tactical adjustment that moved Olise closer to Kylian Mbappe after half-time. His passing range then became the lever that changed the game.

That matters for Chelsea because Alonso’s best Bayer Leverkusen sides were built around players who could receive between lines without killing the tempo. Cole Palmer already gives Chelsea one version of that.

The wider question is whether the squad has another attacker who can bend matches from the opposite side without turning every possession into a one-v-one.

Olise’s Chelsea connection can easily become sentimental. The sharper editorial point is structural.

This is the calibre of player who once passed through the academy pathway and later became a global-level attacker elsewhere. Chelsea cannot change that history, but they can use it to stress-test the next wave of decisions.

That matters for Tyrique George, Kendry Paez, Estevao and any new wide signing.

ReadChelsea has already looked at how Tyrique George’s likely Everton return gives Alonso a fresh winger audit. Olise’s current standing raises the standard of that discussion.

He is no longer just a former academy name or a missed Premier League target. He is evidence of what happens when technical security, role clarity and patience meet elite coaching.

For Alonso, that is the real value of the Olise noise.

Chelsea do not need to turn every academy exit into regret. They do need to recognise the standard now being set by one of Cobham’s former pupils.

The next wide forward who gets serious minutes at Stamford Bridge has to be assessed against that ceiling, not against the safer language of potential.

#2086. “Quite simply disgusting”: Gary Neville tears into Manchester United over Carrick sacking

Graeme Hanna is the site lead of Read Rangers and also writes about West Ham for Read West Ham. A Rangers season-ticket holder and freelance writer, he has previously written for Vital Rangers, Rangers Review, Football Ground Guide and Give Me Sport, and has a long association with the Follow Follow fanzine.

Gary Neville has launched a furious attack on Manchester United’s leadership over the way the club handled Michael Carrick’s dismissal.

United confirmed on Thursday that Carrick had been sacked, four days after the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa left them 18th in the Premier League with eight points from 10 games.

The club said it had reached the “extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary”.

Neville had already branded the process “classless” on The Overlap’s Stick to Football podcast before the announcement, pointing out that it was widely known Carrick was about to go while United were holding talks with potential replacements.

Speaking to Sky Sports after the decision was confirmed, the former United captain went even further.

“It’s just quite simply disgusting,” he said.

“That falls well below the standard of what you would expect in any other business, in any other industry. It would be constructive dismissal and you’d be getting sued.”

Neville took particular aim at the decision to hold the crucial meeting in Monaco, with chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox flying out to meet Sir Jim Ratcliffe while Carrick was still taking training at Carrington.

“The optics of being in Monaco whilst the team, the staff, the people who are running the club on a day-to-day basis are in Manchester, it’s just not good and it reflects badly on the leadership,” he said.

It seems the only ones not to realise that are the trio above, but they aren’t stupid. How they explain it, or attempt to rationalise, it will be painful to listen to.

Neville also argued the club should have acted sooner. Looking back to the 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth in October, he said United “effectively watched Michael Carrick resign on the pitch” as he waved goodbye to supporters at full time, only for the board to hand him three more games.

He summed up the episode as “indecision, lack of authority, just basically really poor leadership”.

It’s more than an episode, it’s an omnishambles that reflects the dysfunctional state of MUFC in its current guise.

United are now expected to move quickly for Mauricio Pochettino. The United States head coach is reported to have reached an agreement in principle with the club, which is prepared to pay his release clause.

First, they will need to wait until the USMNT completes its CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final double header against Haiti on Saturday and Wednesday.

Yes. Man United to wait until an international break to appoint an international manager…

For Neville, though, the bigger problem lies above the dugout and no manager can be the scapegoat for that massive issue.

#2085. BREAKING: Mauricio Pochettino agrees Manchester United deal to become new manager

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United have confirmed an agreement with Mauricio Pochettino to become their next head coach, with the Argentine set to take charge after the international break.

The 54-year-old will replace Michael Carrick, who was dismissed on Thursday following United’s disastrous start to the Premier League season. Pochettino is set to sign a two-and-a-half-year contract that will keep him at Old Trafford until the summer of 2029.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea boss is currently managing the United States national team but is expected to fly straight to Manchester after completing his USA international games.

Pochettino will first oversee the USA’s CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final ties against Haiti on Saturday and next Tuesday. He is expected to arrive in Manchester on Wednesday before taking charge of the club on Thursday.

Pochettino’s first taste of action as a United manager will be against Liverpool at Anfield on November 22.

Pochettino brings considerable Premier League experience after previous spells with Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea. He has also managed Paris Saint-Germain before the USA job.

His appointment makes him Manchester United’s eighth permanent manager since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013.

Carrick’s departure came less than six months after he signed a two-year contract. His second spell in charge ended after United managed just one win in their opening 10 league matches, leaving them in the relegation zone.

Carrick’s coaching staff, including Jonny Evans, Jonathan Woodgate, Steve Holland, Travis Binnion and goalkeeping coach Craig Mawson, have all left alongside Carrick.

#2084. Chelsea Could Claim Share of £164m Compensation

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Chelsea fans have followed Manchester City’s financial rules case for years. Everyone at Stamford Bridge knows a guilty verdict could cost City serious money, and much of it could end up with rivals lower down the table.

Reports now suggest an independent panel has reached a decision. If that holds up, the scale of any Chelsea Manchester City compensation payout could run into tens of millions of pounds for the Blues alone.

The Premier League charged Manchester City with 115 alleged breaches of financial regulations in February 2023. That followed a four-year investigation into the club’s accounts. The case has hung over the competition ever since. Every top-flight club knows the outcome could change how recent Premier League seasons are remembered.

This matters directly to Chelsea. If City are found to have broken spending and disclosure rules, clubs who finished below them could argue they lost out on prize money and European qualification. Chelsea have competed directly with City for top four places and cup competitions throughout that period.

According to The Athletic, Manchester City were found guilty on all but one of the 115 charges by the independent panel. The Premier League has not confirmed the verdict or issued a statement.

Manchester City have not accepted any suggestion of guilt. The club released a statement addressing the ongoing process directly.

“The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such, Manchester City FC’s position remains consistent with the Club’s statement of February 2023. ‘The Club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.'”

That statement makes clear the club does not see the case as settled. Until the Premier League confirms a result, the reported verdict will linger on for official sentencing.

Data specialists at OLBG have estimated the potential Chelsea Manchester City compensation windfall if City are found guilty. They believe City could owe domestic rivals well over £500m in lost Premier League prize money if the charges are proven.

Within that total, London clubs are said to be due around £164m between them. Chelsea, Arsenal and Tottenham Hotspur are among the clubs who could be entitled to a share. Other Premier League sides could benefit too, depending on where they finished compared with City in the seasons in question.

Prize money in the Premier League is tied closely to league position. If City gained points unfairly, that would have pushed a rival down the table and cost them money too. That is the basis for the OLBG figures, and it explains why the sums involved are so large.

For Chelsea, even a share of that £164m pot would be a big boost. It could help fund new signings, or simply ease the pressure around the kind of transfer valuations at Stamford Bridge the club faces every window.

City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak has already made clear the case is far from finished. He described the process as having “a long way to run.” That points to appeals and further legal steps, whatever the panel has decided.

Chelsea, for their part, carry on with life under Xabi Alonso regardless of how the case unfolds. Attention stays on squad rotation and Xabi Alonso’s squad management strategy, not on any potential windfall. The financial case will not change anything on the pitch in the short term.

The Premier League has stayed silent on the reported verdict, and confidentiality remains strict around the process, according to reports from Football.London. Chelsea fans should expect a long wait before any compensation, if it comes at all, reaches the club’s accounts.

#2083. Jamie Gittens suffers Chelsea injury blow with England U21s

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Jamie Gittens has withdrawn from the England Under-21 squad. He suffered an ankle injury during Tuesday’s qualifier against Kazakhstan at Molineux. The Chelsea winger left the ground on crutches. He has returned to Stamford Bridge, where the Jamie Gittens injury will now be assessed by the club’s medical staff.

Gittens picked up the knock after a challenge during the second half of England’s win over Kazakhstan. He was withdrawn as a precaution. He did not take any further part in the match. England have been careful not to overstate the issue and no further reports have come out further.

The 21-year-old struggled to put weight on the affected ankle and was seen limping around Molineux after full time. That prompted an immediate release back to his club, rather than any attempt to assess him further in camp.

England Under-21 boss Lee Carsley addressed the injury directly after the game. He confirmed the nature of the knock and the decision to send Gittens home.

“Jamie got a kick on his ankle,” Carsley said after the match. “We never take any risks. With the age of these players, we don’t ever keep them in camp to see how they are. He will go back.”

England’s statement on the squad changes, detailed in a report from Football.London, confirmed the wider fallout from the fixture.

“Mukasa’s call-up follows the withdrawal of Chelsea’s Jamie Gittens and Norwich City pair Kellen Fisher and Ben Chrisene through injury,” the statement read. West Ham midfielder Divine Mukasa has been called up as cover for all three.

Gittens has been an unused substitute in every Premier League fixture Chelsea have played this season, with his only two appearances under Xabi Alonso coming in the Carabao Cup. Those minutes have offered him little platform after his big summer move.

Alonso’s squad selection has been a talking point since he took charge. Our earlier look at Xabi Alonso’s squad choices at Stamford Bridge covered how competitive things have become. An ankle injury will not change his pecking order in the short term. It does, though, remove any chance of him pushing his case this week.

Chelsea’s break has brought other headlines too. Cole Palmer also withdrew, for entirely different reasons, after his recall by senior boss Thomas Tuchel to the full England squad. Chelsea will be watching both returns closely before domestic football resumes.

Chelsea have not yet issued a formal update on the severity of the injury. Any recovery timeline will depend on an assessment by the club’s medical team once Gittens is back at Cobham. Nothing beyond the crutches seen at Molineux has been confirmed.

Given his limited game time this season, the immediate concern is less about missed fixtures than a setback to his integration under Alonso. Fans can follow how the squad shapes up before the next fixtures through our recent line-up updates. Further news on Gittens is expected once Chelsea’s medical staff finish their evaluation.

West Ham midfielder Tomáš Souček has admitted that the players must take their share of responsibility for the club’s disappointing Championship campaign, insisting that changing the manager doesn’t absolve them of blame.

Speaking to Czech publication Sport.cz, Souček acknowledged that results and performances haven’t been good enough and that West Ham must rediscover their winning mentality. He also made it clear that failing to return to the Premier League would represent failure.

It’s difficult to disagree with that sentiment, although I would argue that there wasn’t an awful lot wrong with the players’ attitudes during the 2-1 defeat against Blackburn Rovers. Most of them appeared to be trying their best, and there were periods when West Ham attacked well down both flanks.

Mads Hermansen had something of a nightmare in goal, while Manor Solomon was ineffective when introduced from the bench. But I don’t think the overall performance was primarily a question of effort or attitude, which is why I’d argue that Scott Parker is the man who needs to fix things through better instruction and some new tactics.

As for Souček himself, there was a point during the Blackburn game when I thought we were crying out for his goalscoring ability. West Ham really only have two proven goalscorers in Jarrod Bowen and Tomáš Souček, and I felt the Czech midfielder should have been introduced much earlier.

Even in his brief appearance, Souček managed to get himself into a good goalscoring position, although his late header was saved. It was another reminder of something West Ham have been missing, particularly when the forwards have struggled to make an impact.

Souček is right that the players have a responsibility to improve, but from what I saw at Ewood Park, I don’t think a lack of effort was the biggest problem. Parker now has the international break to work on the team’s organisation and tactics, and that’s where I’d expect to see the most significant improvement.
