#1921. ‘Should be’ - Leeds United urged to target Middlesbrough FC marksman Will Lankshear by ex-Premier League scout

A former Premier League scout believes Leeds United should set their sights on Middlesbrough marksman Will Lankshear.

The 21-year-old only joined Middlesbrough in the summer, sealing a move from Tottenham Hotspur for an initial fee reported to be in the £10m region.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

He has made a stunning start to life at the Riverside, notching 15 goals across his first 16 appearances in the club’s colours.

His scinillating form has fuelled talk of a potential England call-up - despite the fact he is playing in the second tier.

Mick Brown, a former scout for the likes of Manchester United and Blackburn Rovers, believes Leeds should be among those on his trail.

He told Football Insider: “Will Lankshear is obviously going to have a lot of Premier League clubs looking at him. He's proving already he's a top-class striker, it's not like he's just come out of nowehere, he's somebody these clubs have been aware of even when he was at Tottenham.

“But now he's showing he can do it at a high level, there's even been talk of an England call-up, so maybe he is ready for the Premier League.

“He's a certain type of striker, a penalty box striker, somebody who gets on the end of moves and scores goals rather than getting involved too much, and Leeds could do with a player like that.

“Whether or not he'll be allowed to leave in January, there could be offers to tempt him away, because why not? Why not test their resolve?

“Leeds should be one of those clubs interested, but obviously they won't be the only one, so it's going to be something to keep an eye on.”

Middlesbrough will be determined to hold on to Lankshear, especially considering they are firmly in the Championship promotion picture.

However, the lure of the Premier League often proves strong for the second tier’s leading lights. Leeds sit ninth in the Premier League table and currently have Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Lukas Nmecha as their forward options.

#1920. Chelsea urged to sign Trent Alexander-Arnold amid Liverpool return rumours

Chelsea have been urged to sign ‘top-class’ Trent Alexander-Arnold in January following a frustrating start to his Real Madrid career.

Alexander-Arnold completed a dream move to Madrid last year, ending a 21-year spell at boyhood club Liverpool in which he won two Premier League titles and the Champions League.

The England international featured in a little over half of Real Madrid’s league games last season as the Spanish giants endured a rare trophyless campaign.

Competition at right-back only increased over the summer with the arrival of Denzel Dumfries from Inter Milan and Jose Mourinho is currently playing midfielder Federico Valverde in that position.

As a result Alexander-Arnold appears to be third choice and has only earned four starts this season, with his lack of game-time raising speculation over his future at the Bernabeu.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

A return to Liverpool has been raised as a potential possibility given his former club’s issues at right-back, but Glen Johnson has urged Chelsea to bring the 28-year-old to Stamford Bridge.

Chelsea’s first-choice right-back, club captain Reece James, is expected to be out of action until at least mid-January after undergoing knee surgery last month.

‘Trent Alexander-Arnold will definitely be frustrated playing such a small role at Real Madrid this season,’ ex-Liverpool and Chelsea defender Johnson told SeatPick.

‘Before he went to Madrid, he would have planned on nailing down his spot at right back there, and then they brought in a new right back the summer after he arrived, which will have only frustrated him further.

‘Trent is a top-class player, and no top-class player wants to sit on the bench, he wants to be playing regular football.

Liverpool legend Steven Gerrard recently said he would welcome Alexander-Arnold back to Anfield despite the fact his exit upset many fans.

#1919. Tottenham transfer news: Spurs 'join' Arsenal in race for £40m talisman scoring every 85 minutes

By Lewis Blain | 12 Nov 2026 07:38

Tottenham Hotspur have joined arch-rivals Arsenal in the race to sign AC Monza striker Gustavo Varela ahead of the January transfer window.

The 21-year-old has enjoyed a remarkable rise over the past year, becoming one of Serie A's most prolific forwards despite playing for a struggling side.

However, Spurs and their rivals could face a battle to convince Monza to part with their prized asset midway through the season.

According to reports in Portugal (via Sport Witness), Tottenham, Juventus and Inter Milan have all joined the growing list of clubs monitoring Varela.

Arsenal were already keeping tabs on the striker, alongside Napoli and LaLiga giants Barcelona, meaning competition for his signature is increasing.

Spurs have not submitted an offer or opened formal negotiations, with their interest currently at the monitoring stage.

Monza are reluctant to sell in January, viewing Varela as essential to their fight against relegation. It is believed that the Italian side could demand up to €50m (£42m).

Varela's rise has been particularly impressive.

Having struggled for regular opportunities during a loan spell at Gil Vicente, he eventually established himself in the first team last January, finishing the campaign with seven goals and three assists in 33 appearances.

His move to Monza during the summer has taken his career to another level, with the forward scoring 11 goals in 11 games this season, finding the net once every 85 minutes despite the club sitting 18th in Serie A on just seven points. He has also earned his first senior Portugal call-up under Jorge Jesus.

Those numbers make it easy to understand why so many clubs are taking notice.

Varela has even attracted comparisons with former Chelsea and Wolves striker Diego Costa, adding another intriguing dimension to his growing reputation.

For Tottenham, the appeal is obvious, as the Portuguese talisman could offer a much-needed attacking option, while Arsenal and Barceona's interest suggests his performances are attracting attention well beyond Italy.

However, spending upwards of £42m on a striker with only a short period of senior-level consistency would represent a considerable investment.

His extraordinary scoring rate makes him an exciting prospect, but Monza's reluctance to sell means January could prove a difficult time to secure his signature.

#1918. How Manchester United could line up in Mauricio Pochettino’s first game vs Liverpool

Mauricio Pochettino is officially set to become the next Manchester United manager, and his first game will come just days after his start date.

The Red Devils return from the final international break of 2026 to face the daunting prospect of visiting arch-rivals Liverpool in the Premier League on Sunday, November 22.

Pochettino inherits a side with just one win in 10 top-flight games this term, a string of results that have left Man Utd in the relegation zone.

The Argentine’s style of play centres around a high-press and an ability to build from the back - two things United have struggled with so far this season.

Injuries across the pitch will impact Pochettino’s selection, with Carlos Baleba and Benjamin Sesko definitely ruled out for the trip to Anfield.

In goal, Senne Lammens is established first-choice and that is unlikely to change with Pochettino’s arrival.

Interestingly, Pochettino might be tempted to copy Carrick and play Leny Yoro at right-back. Out of possession the right-back tucks in to form a three-man defence in Pochettino’s favoured system, but with an actual left-back fit, there is little reason to play defenders out of position.

For that reason, Diogo Dalot will likely start at right-back, with a much more simple defensive approach. Yoro and Ayden Heaven in the heart of defence could give United a bit more pace than a backline featuring Harry Maguire, but the experience of Lisandro Martinez may be hard to ignore as Pochettino balances a squad lacking in confidence.

Patrick Dorgu seems a strong fit at left-back. Antonee Robinson loved to get forward for Pochettino while on USA duty, and the wing-back is a proven attacking threat.

With the USA, Pochettino has settled on a 4-3-3 formation, with the midfield featuring a sitting player behind two more proactive team-mates.

Man Utd appoint Mauricio Pochettino as manager on two-and-a-half year deal

Pochettino has already decided his first two Man Utd signings

When will Pochettino start as Man Utd manager?

Pochettino’s immediate issue with the United squad will be the fact that there is no clear candidate as a holding midfielder. The injured Baleba does well at screening the backline, but his strengths rely on driving forward with the ball.

It is a similar story for Andrey Santos - a midfielder that is still unsure whether his best position is as a No6, 8, or 10.

The deep-lying playmaker role is a battle between Kobbie Mainoo and Youri Tielemans. Pochettino has shown a tendency to trust young, talented players, so it would not be a surprise to see the former Tottenham manager try and work his magic with Mainoo.

Tielemans could play the box-to-box role alongside Mainoo, offering experience during the transition to Pochettino’s ideal approach.

While Pochettino has utilised a deeper player in the middle of the park with the USA, it is likely that he will instead have to build a more attacking midfield at United.

That is because club captain Bruno Fernandes is clearly the Red Devils’ best player, which merits his inclusion.

Matheus Cunha looks a good fit on the left wing as a creative spark, while Bryan Mbeumo’s pace down the right wing would allow Pochettino to create a similar attacking shape to his USA side.

However, with United’s striking options limited, it would not be a surprise to see Mbeumo lead the line, with Amad Diallo playing instead on the right.

Predicted Manchester United XI vs Liverpool (4-2-3-1): Lammens; Dalot, Yoro, Martinez, Dorgu; Tielemans, Mainoo; Amad, Fernandes, Cunha; Mbeumo

#1917. Mikel Arteta urged to sell £60m Arsenal star in swap deal for Julian Alvarez

Alan Smith believes that Arsenal should consider offering Martin Zubimendi to Atletico Madrid as part of a swap deal to sign Julian Alvarez.

Zubimendi’s future at Arsenal has come into question in recent weeks, with the Spaniard still yet to start a Premier League match this season.

The central midfielder made an immediate impact after signing from Real Sociedad for £60million 18 months ago, starting 34 matches as Mikel Arteta’s side ended their 22-year wait for another league title.

Fatigue, however, eventually caught up with Zubimendi at the end of last season and his place was effectively taken by teenager Myles Lewis-Skelly, who started in his place in the Champions League final.

Lewis-Skelly’s continued form, as well as the high-profile summer arrival of Bruno Guimaraes, has seen Zubimendi slide down the pecking order in north London and sparked speculation that a January move could be on the cards for the World Cup winner.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Atletico Madrid are reportedly keen to bring Zubimendi back to La Liga, and Smith believes the Gunners can use that interest to finally strike a deal for Alvarez, who they were heavily interested in over the summer.

‘Obviously he played a big part last season, but having been an ever-present, he might be getting a bit restless not to be getting starts, just to be coming off the bench for a few minutes, Smith told Best Betting Sites.

‘So that might be something that can be part of a bargaining chip for Arsenal.

‘If you could do a part swap, then obviously you’re not shelling out over 100 million pounds on Alvarez, because I’m sure Atletico would want something well in excess of that. So that might be a way forward.
